title: Two Sum
statement_md:
Given an array of integers `nums` and an integer `target`, return indices of the two numbers such that they add up to `target`.

You may assume that each input would have **exactly one solution**, and you may not use the same element twice.

You can return the answer in any order.

hints.text: Can you check if the complement (target - current) exists?
Use a Hash Map to record previously visited numbers and their indices.
As you iterate over `nums`, lookup `target - num` in your dictionary. If found, return `[seen[target - num], i]`. Otherwise store `seen[num] = i`.

editorial_md:
### Optimal Approach: One-Pass Hash Map

Store indices in a map `seen`. At each number `x`, check if `target - x` is in `seen`. If so, return `[seen[target - x], index]`. Otherwise record `seen[x] = index`.

- Time Complexity: $O(n)$
- Space Complexity: $O(n)$
